preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10⁴) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and 1 <= n <= 2 * 10**5 for n in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line after t is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10⁵) representing the length of string s.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n and all(c in '+-' for c in s) for n, s in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the second line is a string s of length n consisting only of '+' and '-' characters.

preconditions.expression: sum(int(n) for n in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]]) <= 2 * 10**5
preconditions.description: The sum of all n across test cases does not exceed 2·10⁵.

postconditions.expression: stdout == '\n'.join(str(count_promising_substrings(s)) for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]) + '\n'
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is a single integer: the count of non-empty promising substrings in s. A substring is promising if it can be made balanced by replacing adjacent '--' with '+' any number of times (including zero). A balanced string has equal counts of '+' and '-'.

postconditions.expression: all(count_promising_substrings(s) == sum(1 for i in range(len(s)) for j in range(i + 1, len(s) + 1) if is_promising(s[i:j])) for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]])
postconditions.description: The count is computed by enumerating all non-empty substrings of s and summing 1 for each substring that is promising. A substring s[i:j] is promising if there exists a sequence of operations (replacing '--' with '+') that transforms it into a balanced string.

postconditions.expression: all(is_promising(substring) == (min_plus_minus(substring) <= 0) for substring in [s[i:j] for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]] for i in range(len(s)) for j in range(i + 1, len(s) + 1)])
postconditions.description: A substring is promising if and only if the minimum possible difference between the number of '+' and '-' signs (after optimally applying operations) is ≤ 0. The operation reduces the count of '-' by 2 and increases '+' by 1 each time, so the difference (plus_count - minus_count) changes by +3 per operation. The minimum difference is computed as: (plus_count - minus_count) - 3 * max_possible_operations, where max_possible_operations is the maximum number of '--' pairs that can be replaced.
